title: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation
meta_description: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation services from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Dataq Software's Agentic AI & Hyperautomation practice: what the tower covers, the services inside it, the platforms it deploys and the outcomes typical programs commit to.

Agentic AI & Hyperautomation turns knowledge work into orchestrated autonomy. We build goal-directed, tool-using agents that operate inside your systems and controls, wire them into human-in-the-loop checkpoints where regulation demands it, and instrument every decision path for later review. The tower spans process and task mining, decision intelligence, intelligent document processing, and the integration layer that lets hundreds of automations run as one governed fleet.

The economics flipped: agent runtimes, evaluation harnesses, and orchestration frameworks are production-grade, while labor costs and error costs keep rising. Boards no longer ask whether to automate — they ask why exception rates are still above 30% and why month-end close still takes nine days when the work is pattern-shaped.

items: Agents that execute the work: tool-using, policy-bounded, and fully logged for audit.
Agents operated as one fleet: roles, queues, budgets and audit trails.
Decision paths that run in milliseconds, with policy checks and full logging.
Contracts, claims and invoices read end-to-end: extraction, validation and downstream action.
See the work as it actually runs: event-log truth before you automate anything.
One automation spine: APIs, events, RPA and agents composable under common control.
Workflows that recover from failure on their own — long-running business processes that adapt, retry and recover without tickets.

blocks.x: Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass carry the production rails for this tower — governance, security posture and audit evidence production are inherited from the platform, so programs harden instead of improvising.

items: P99 under 150 ms for scoring+policy paths

blocks.x: Anchor industries: Banking & Financial Services, Energy & Utilities, Healthcare & Life Sciences, Insurance & Risk, Logistics & Supply Chain, Manufacturing & Industrial, Public Sector & Government, Retail & Consumer Goods, Technology & SaaS, Telecom, Media & Entertainment.

Delivery follows the same weekly rhythm on every program of this type. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
At the end of the first quarter of a typical program you hold four concrete assets:

items: The signed measurement of where the metric stands today, with the method written out so the number can be defended to finance.
Every automated decision path, its policy checks, its human checkpoint and its owner on one page.
Logs, evaluations and approvals collected automatically as the program runs — ready for internal audit or a regulator.
A running record of the delta against baseline, updated at every gate, reviewed at every steering meeting.
